content.text: {"answer":"The closest match is POLO, which targets multi-platform delivery dispatching where couriers work for several platforms but each platform can only observe its own orders and couriers due to privacy/operational constraints. POLO formulates the environment as partially observable multi-agent reinforcement learning and trains each platform-grid pair as an independent agent using only platform-local observations, with an attention-based policy to handle incomplete and heterogeneous courier information. It also uses counterfactual reward shaping to mitigate non-stationarity from joint actions.\n\nOther papers use multi-agent reinforcement learning for delivery-like problems (e.g., ride-sharing order dispatch, UAV medical supply delivery, and integrated pickup dispatch/routing), but they do not specifically address managing couriers who work across multiple apps with partial observability from multiple platforms. For example, Triple-BERT focuses on order dispatch on ride-sharing platforms using centralized single-agent MARL, and does not describe multi-platform privacy-limited observations; UAV-MARL focuses on limited visibility among UAV agents within a POMDP.","grounded":true}
